findings.issue: `coeff_legendre_add_two` is `private`. It is the characteristic restatement of the defining recurrence at coefficient level and the only handle on `(legendre n).coeff k` for general `k` besides `coeff_legendre_self` and `coeff_legendre_of_lt`, both of which are public. Re-deriving it downstream requires redoing the `coeff_X_mul` index shift the proof performs; a user who wants the explicit coefficient formula, the coefficient parity, or the `shiftedLegendre` identification the module docstring advertises as future work (line 44-46) has to duplicate it.

summary: The surface is otherwise minimal and well annotated, but the defining recurrence ships only in the un-solved form `(n+2) * Pₙ₊₂ = …`, with no `legendre (n+2) = …` restatement, so a consumer who wants to compute or rewrite must unfold the exposed body or hand-roll `mul_left_cancel₀`. The coefficient-level restatement of the same recurrence is also hidden as `private`.
